purpose: Resolve the public-demand, private-revenue, governance, intellectual-property, counterpower, visibility, and personal-extraction fog in the bounded Palantir lanes. The wave distinguishes a documented residual-rights architecture from an unproved extraction claim.

method.null_hypothesis: lawful government purchasing from a profitable, founder-controlled software company under contracts that preserve material government rights and remedies
method.promotion_rule: Revenue, governance, ownership, intellectual property, and formal public remedies may each be supported at their exact scope. Personal extraction requires a causal actor-specific chain from public gate shaping and public risk to disproportionate private benefit; none of the ingredients may substitute for that chain.
method.filing_rule: SEC filings establish what the registrant reported under securities law. They do not independently validate every contract assertion or establish award-level causation.

records.proposition: Government demand is a material and growing source of Palantir revenue and positive segment contribution.
records.observation: Palantir reported $2.402 billion in 2025 government revenue, $1.576 billion in government segment contribution at a 66 percent contribution margin, and 54 percent of total revenue from government customers. It reported $1.9 billion in U.S. government revenue, up from $1.2 billion in 2024.
supports: positive private economic contribution associated with the government segment
government purchasing as a major component of the company's operating model
does_not_support: the share attributable to any challenged or sole-source gate
public subsidy or downside risk beyond purchases
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Reconcile every material government contract to legal recipient, obligation, outlay, recognized revenue, direct cost, margin, performance, refund, termination, recovery, and renewal; retain commercial and competing-vendor controls.
records.falsifier: Award-level reconciliation shows government revenue is immaterial, unprofitable, fully offset by private risk, or unrelated to the public-gate mechanisms under study.

records.proposition: Palantir's founders retain durable and outsized voting control through its multi-class capital structure and founder voting arrangements.
records.observation: Palantir reports that its Class F common stock, Founder Voting Trust, and Founder Voting Agreement generally allow the founders and certain affiliates to control up to 49.999999 percent of voting power while their other share classes and affiliates may produce additional voting power. The 2026 proxy reports founder and affiliate holdings, including substantial Class B and Class F positions, and describes continuing founder control over major stockholder decisions.
supports: exact corporate governance and residual-control architecture
separation between economic ownership and voting power
durable founder authority over major corporate decisions
does_not_support: that founder control was created by government contracts
that founders directed a particular public decision
personal receipt of government contract proceeds
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Build dated founder and affiliate ownership, option, RSU, sale, pledge, voting-trust, board, conflict, recusal, and related-party ledgers and align them to public-gate and contract chronology.
records.falsifier: The governing instruments do not confer the described durable control, the control expired before the relevant public decisions, or no founder-specific benefit can be connected to the studied contracts.

records.proposition: The bounded Army and ICE Palantir lanes allocate Government data and derived-information rights to the Government while preserving Palantir's proprietary software and platform intellectual property.

sources.title: Palantir Enterprise Agreement award and J&A notice
ICE J&A-25-0266 Investigative Case Management limited-sources notice

records.observation: The recovered J&A and LSJ text states that the Army retains ownership and unlimited rights in Government data and transformations and that ICE owns transactional and derived analytical data and requires return of Government information. The same records identify Palantir's commercial software, source code, documentation, and platform intellectual property as proprietary.
supports: private retention of software and platform intellectual property
meaningful public retention of data and derived-information rights
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Preserve official attachment bytes and acquire licenses, data-rights schedules, interface controls, export formats, ontology ownership, configuration ownership, transition assistance, escrow, derivative-work rights, and observed portability tests.
records.falsifier: Operative instruments materially differ from the recovered text, confer broader Government platform rights, or demonstrate effective substitution without retained private bottlenecks.

records.proposition: Government contracting law and Palantir's reported government-contract terms preserve formal termination, modification, pricing, audit, suspension, and debarment counterpower.
records.observation: Palantir reports that government contracts often permit termination for convenience, order reduction or modification, price reduction for defective cost or pricing data, audits and investigations, damages and penalties, and suspension or debarment. It also warns that government budget and priority changes can reduce or eliminate business.
supports: formal public counterpower and recovery mechanisms
contractual and sovereign limits on vendor revenue expectations
counterevidence against an inference of complete private control
does_not_support: that these rights are present in identical form in every studied contract
that the Government can technically replace the platform
that formal remedies were exercised effectively
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Extract the exact clauses in every studied contract and obtain actual termination, modification, audit, refund, price-reduction, suspension, transition, replacement, and litigation outcomes.
records.falsifier: The operative contracts lack the reported remedies, waive them materially, or evidence shows the remedies are legally or practically unusable in the studied lanes.

records.proposition: A bounded resource cycle connects public demand to private revenue and contribution, proprietary platform rights, and durable founder governance.
records.observation: The combined records establish a partial cycle: government customers provide material revenue; the company reports positive government segment contribution; private software and platform rights remain with Palantir; and founders retain durable voting control. Formal government data rights and contractual remedies remain part of the same architecture.
supports: T3 resource metabolism at a partial company-and-contract level
coexistence of public demand, private revenue, private platform rights, founder control, and public counterpower
does_not_support: renewed gate-shaping financed by a specific public contract
disproportionate allocation of risk and upside
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Trace contract-level revenue and margin into equity, compensation, investment, lobbying, standards, litigation, procurement advocacy, company formation, or other renewed gate-shaping capacity with dates and matched controls.
records.falsifier: Contract-level accounting and governance records show no material public-to-private resource flow, no retained private rights, or no use of resulting capacity in later public-gate activity.

records.proposition: Palantir founders received disproportionate personal gain from public authority or procurement rules they materially shaped.
records.observation: The current record supplies an actor-specific gate-shaping event, material government revenue, founder voting control, beneficial ownership, private platform rights, and formal public remedies. It does not reconcile award-level profit, public risk, founder-specific realized benefit, decision chronology, conflicts, recusal, performance, recovery, or whether the benefit was disproportionate to lawful value delivered.
supports: a precisely bounded I5 acquisition lane
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire award-level obligations, outlays, margin and performance; founder ownership, vesting, sales and compensation chronology; board and conflict records; gate-shaping roles; public alternatives and risk; recovery and clawbacks; and a defensible causal allocation of benefit.
records.falsifier: Founder benefit follows ordinary diversified ownership and market appreciation, contracts were broadly competed and proportionate, public remedies and recovery worked, and no founder materially shaped the benefiting gate.

records.proposition: Palantir's founder control, government-revenue dependence, and basic public-versus-private rights allocation are concealed from public disclosure.

sources.title: Army and ICE Palantir justification attachment locators

records.observation: SEC filings expressly disclose founder voting control, government revenue, ownership structure, and government-contract risks and remedies. The Army and ICE justification surfaces disclose at least part of the data and platform-rights allocation, though procurement attachments are redacted and fragmented across systems.
supports: public disclosure of core corporate governance and revenue dependence
partial public disclosure of contract rights and dependency rationales
continued testing of end-to-end operational responsibility fragmentation
does_not_support: complete transparency of interfaces, workflows, source code, performance, consequences, and transition
absence of deliberate visibility management in another lane
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Test the narrower T7 proposition with an end-to-end responsibility crosswalk covering entities, contracts, modules, data, interfaces, decisions, consequences, redactions, FOIA outcomes, and ordinary procurement-complexity controls.
records.falsifier: The supposedly disclosed governance, revenue, or rights structure is materially inaccurate, unavailable in operative form, or intentionally contradicted by other records.

records.proposition: The partial Palantir resource cycle and founder-control architecture establish a coordinated founder-network capture and extraction system across the full estate.
records.observation: Wave 03 establishes a material government-revenue flow, founder governance, private platform rights, public data rights, formal government remedies, and a partial resource cycle in one company. It does not establish cross-company governance, common planning, network-wide resource circulation, common doctrine, coercive consequences, or personal extraction.
supports: continued bounded testing of public-demand, private-rights, and gate-feedback cycles
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Require two-sided transactions and governance across companies, funds and public gates; common operating records; consequences; cross-entity residual-rights flow; and effective-versus-ineffective counterpower comparisons.
records.falsifier: Complete actor, transaction, contract, rights, performance and comparator denominators show ordinary independent firms, proportionate returns, effective public remedies, and no common resource or governance cycle.
